subject: pathology
title: Amyloidosis: types, staining and organ patterns

steps.tx: Amyloid is abnormal protein that deposits outside cells and distorts normal tissue. **Amyloid** forms beta pleated sheets, and **Congo red staining** with apple green birefringence identifies deposits under polarised light. Precise typing of the precursor protein is essential because treatment differs completely between the major amyloid types.
steps.say: Amyloid is misfolded protein and it is deposited outside cells in tissues. The deposits are beta pleated sheets and they resist normal breakdown in tissue. Congo red staining is diagnostic because apple green birefringence appears under polarised light. Typing is essential because treatment differs completely by type.

vis.alt: Microscopic image showing amyloid deposits stained with Congo red, then exhibiting apple-green birefringence under polarized light.
vis.caption: Congo red staining and apple green birefringence identify amyloid. Image: Marvin 101, CC BY 3.0, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.tx: AL amyloidosis is caused by immunoglobulin light chains from a plasma cell clone. **AL amyloidosis** commonly involves the heart and kidney, and **macroglossia** is a useful clinical clue. Serum free light chains detect the clone, and therapy targets the abnormal plasma cells that produce the precursor protein.
steps.say: AL amyloidosis is caused by light chains from a clonal plasma cell population. The heart, kidney, liver and nerves are commonly involved in this disease. Macroglossia is a useful clue and restrictive heart disease develops in many patients. Therapy is directed against the plasma cell clone itself.

left.title: AL amyloidosis
points: Light chain precursor from plasma cell clone
Heart, kidney, nerve and gut dominant

right.title: AA amyloidosis
points: Serum amyloid A precursor from chronic inflammation

steps.tx: AA amyloidosis follows prolonged inflammation and mainly damages the kidney. **AA amyloidosis** develops from serum amyloid A protein, and **chronic inflammation** from arthritis, infection or bowel disease drives its production. Renal involvement causes heavy proteinuria, whereas cardiac involvement is less prominent than in AL disease.
steps.say: AA amyloidosis develops after years of uncontrolled chronic inflammation in the body. Serum amyloid A is the precursor and it is raised during persistent inflammation. The kidney is damaged most often and heavy proteinuria develops progressively. Controlling inflammation is important because it reduces precursor production.

steps.tx: Organ involvement produces patterns that examiners combine into clinical stems. Cardiac amyloid causes **voltage mass mismatch** with thick walls and low voltage, and renal amyloid causes **nephrotic proteinuria** without active sediment. Peripheral and autonomic neuropathy also occur, and periorbital purpura reflects fragile vessels in affected tissue.
steps.say: Cardiac amyloid causes thick ventricular walls with low voltage on electrocardiography. Renal amyloid is important because nephrotic proteinuria occurs without active urinary sediment. Neuropathy and autonomic failure are common and they cause significant disability. The voltage and mass mismatch is a highly tested clue.

rows: Thick wall with low ECG voltage
Diabetic neuropathy is slower and length dependent

steps.tx: This electrocardiogram shows the classic cardiac clue in amyloidosis. Limb leads show **low voltage** complexes, and the chest leads show a **pseudoinfarct pattern** without true infarction. When thick walls are present on echocardiography, this mismatch strongly suggests amyloid infiltration and is a favourite pattern in examination stems.
steps.say: This tracing shows small QRS complexes in the limb leads clearly. A pseudoinfarct pattern is present in the early chest leads without infarction. Cardiac amyloid causes this pattern because infiltrated walls generate low voltage. Thick walls on echocardiography make the mismatch highly significant.

vis.caption: Twelve lead ECG showing low limb lead voltage and pseudoinfarct pattern. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Transthyretin amyloidosis mainly affects older adults and often involves the heart. **Transthyretin amyloidosis** can be hereditary or wild type, and **carpal tunnel syndrome** can precede cardiac disease by years. Abdominal fat pad aspiration provides a minimally invasive biopsy site, and dialysis related amyloid is now less common.
steps.say: Transthyretin amyloidosis affects older adults and it commonly involves the heart. Carpal tunnel syndrome is important because it precedes cardiac disease by years. The disease is hereditary in some families and wild type in others. Fat pad aspiration is useful because it is minimally invasive.
